properties.name: Two or more of a person's designs can be compared on one topic, on demand: each design's topic neighbourhood is assembled under its own namespace and reported side by side, with the judgement left to the agent
properties.statement:
A tool (a topic_report that takes `designs`, or a compare_topic) takes a topic and a list of designs the caller may read, gathers each design's topic neighbourhood as topic_report does (search hits and their edges), assembles them under namespaces as compose_and_analyse does, and reports side by side: what one design holds on the topic and another lacks; requirements, decisions, constraints and interfaces whose statements match closely (the family check's similarity scoring, at a stated threshold); declared interfaces or constraints that disagree; and what neither declares. It never opens more than the neighbourhoods, so it is cheap on demand. The reply says that a near-match is a candidate for the agent's or the person's judgement, never a finding of sameness (measured 2026-10-09: a similarity sweep at 0.4 finds a true duplicate one time in eight). Designs the caller cannot read are left out and named as such. On flo2.io the host runs it for hosted designs (flo2's req:flo2-io-assembles-a-hubs-designs-into-one-graph-when-asked); locally the person's reflow2 runs it over designs it can open.
Anthony, 2026-10-10: "would it be more a 'oauth 2 keys:values' in flo2 <-compared-> 'oauth 2 keys:values' in storyflow? I'd imagine these types of operations at the key:value level could be done very rapidly and on demand?" He kept option (b) of dec:idea-two-designs-are-compared-on-one-topic-on-demand. Kept beside it: speed is bounded by opening each design, not by scanning; this needs no pin between the designs.
